chunks: 1823 - Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:
"Whoever fasts during Sha‘ban, it will be a purification for him from every slip, stain, and impulsive act."
Abu Hamzah said: "So I said to Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام: 'What is al-wasmah?' He said: 'An oath in disobedience, and a vow; and there is no vow in disobedience.'"
I said: "Then what is al-badirah?" He said: "An oath made in anger, and repentance from it is regret over it."

key_terms.النَّدَمُ: Regret, identified here as the repentance for such an act.
key_terms.الْبَادِرَةُ: A rash or impulsive act, explained here as an oath uttered in anger.
key_terms.الْغَضَبِ: Anger, the state in which a rash oath may be made.
key_terms.الْمَعْصِيَةِ: Disobedience to Allah, in which no valid vow is recognized.
key_terms.زَلَّةٍ: A slip or lapse into error.
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: The month of Sha‘ban, in which fasting is being encouraged here.
key_terms.طَهُورًا: A means of purification from sins and moral faults.
key_terms.وَصْمَةُ: A moral stain, explained here as an oath or vow connected to disobedience.

ai.seo_question: How does fasting in Sha‘ban purify a person from sins and rash behavior?
ai.summary: This hadith states that fasting in Sha‘ban serves as a purification from slips, moral blemishes, and rash actions. It also explains that sinful oaths and vows have no validity in disobedience, and that repentance for an oath uttered in anger is sincere remorse.
